questions.question: What is cobalt and why does the body need it?
questions.answer: Cobalt is an essential trace metal, meaning the body requires small amounts of it. Its essential role comes from being the central metal atom in vitamin B12, according to [[sources/ufelle2021-metals-chapter|Ufelle & Barchowsky 2021]].

questions.question: What health effects can cobalt cause?
questions.answer: The attached toxicology source notes that cobalt-containing dusts and hard-metal materials can produce respiratory toxicity, allergic dermatitis, cardiomyopathy, and carcinogenicity concerns [[sources/ufelle2021-metals-chapter|Ufelle & Barchowsky 2021]]. The page does not quantify these effects or tie them to specific dietary exposures.

questions.question: Which forms of cobalt are associated with toxicity?
questions.answer: The page attributes cobalt's toxic effects specifically to cobalt-containing dusts and hard-metal (hard-metal/tungsten-carbide) materials rather than to cobalt in general [[sources/ufelle2021-metals-chapter|Ufelle & Barchowsky 2021]]. It does not describe toxicity thresholds or food-specific exposure levels.

questions.question: How much does this page currently tell me about cobalt in food?
questions.answer: Very little. This is a source-map stub created during the re-ingest of [[sources/ufelle2021-metals-chapter|Ufelle & Barchowsky 2021]], and it states that substantive, cobalt-specific expansion awaits a dedicated cobalt ingest. At present it carries only a general characterization of cobalt and a single attached toxicology source.
